title: If a bhikkhu possesses six qualities, bhikkhus, whether by day or by night, a decline in wholesome states is to be expected, not growth. What…
content: If a bhikkhu possesses six qualities, bhikkhus, whether by day or by night, a decline in wholesome states is to be expected, not growth. What six? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has great desires, is discontented, is not satisfied with any kind of basic necessities such as robes, almsfood, lodgings, medicinal requisites; he has no faith, is immoral, is lazy, has forgetful mindfulness, and has evil wisdom.

title: And, Aggivessana, what is the trained body and what is the trained mind? Here, Aggivessana, a learned noble disciple experiences a pleasant feeling. Experiencing a…
content: And, Aggivessana, what is the trained body and what is the trained mind? Here, Aggivessana, a learned noble disciple experiences a pleasant feeling. Experiencing a pleasant feeling, he is not attached to that pleasant feeling, does not fall into attachment to it. If that pleasant feeling ceases, with the cessation of the pleasant feeling, a painful feeling arises. Experiencing that painful feeling, he does not sorrow, grieve, lament, beat his breast, or become confused. Aggivessana, that pleasant feeling that arose for that person does not invade his mind and does not remain — because the body is trained. That painful feeling that arose for that person does not invade his mind and does not remain — because the mind is trained. Aggivessana, in whatever person, both ways, a pleasant feeling arises, does not invade the mind and does not remain — because the body is trained; a painful feeling arises, does not invade the mind and does not remain — because the mind is trained. Thus, Aggivessana, that person is one with a trained body and a trained mind.

title: - Just as, bhikkhus, a stick thrown up into the sky sometimes falls on its base, sometimes in the middle, sometimes on its tip. So…
content: - Just as, bhikkhus, a stick thrown up into the sky sometimes falls on its base, sometimes in the middle, sometimes on its tip. So too, bhikkhus, beings shrouded by ignorance and fettered by craving, wandering and roaming on, sometimes go from this world to another world, sometimes from another world to this world. Why is that? Because they do not see the Four Noble Truths. What four? The Noble Truth of Suffering ... the Noble Truth of the Path leading to the Cessation of Suffering.

title: 'Everything exists,' Kaccāyana, is one extreme. 'Nothing exists' is the second extreme. Avoiding both extremes, Kaccāyana, the Tathāgata teaches the Dhamma by the middle way.…
content: 'Everything exists,' Kaccāyana, is one extreme. 'Nothing exists' is the second extreme. Avoiding both extremes, Kaccāyana, the Tathāgata teaches the Dhamma by the middle way. With ignorance as condition, formations arise; with formations as condition, consciousness ... Thus is the origination of this whole mass of suffering. But with the complete fading away and cessation of ignorance, formations cease; with the cessation of formations, consciousness ceases ... Thus is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.

title: The forest of sensual desires arises from association; it is cut down by non-association. Just as a small plank of wood sinks in the great…
content:
The forest of sensual desires arises from association; it is cut down by non-association. Just as a small plank of wood sinks in the great river, so does a good person sink when associating with a lazy person. Therefore, avoid the lazy, the unenergetic.

Dwell with the noble seers,
The secluded, the diligent,
Those devoted to jhāna,
Ever ardent and mindful.

title: Like a tortoise drawing its limbs Into its own shell, So too, a bhikkhu, Gathering all his thoughts, Not dependent on anyone, Not harming anyone,…
content:
Like a tortoise drawing its limbs
Into its own shell,
So too, a bhikkhu,
Gathering all his thoughts,
Not dependent on anyone,
Not harming anyone,
Fully at peace,
Criticizing no one.

title: Here, Mahānāma, a noble disciple has shame, feeling ashamed of bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, mental misconduct, feeling ashamed of having evil, unwholesome states. He has…
content: Here, Mahānāma, a noble disciple has shame, feeling ashamed of bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, mental misconduct, feeling ashamed of having evil, unwholesome states. He has fear, feeling afraid of bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, mental misconduct, feeling afraid of having evil, unwholesome states.

title: Then the Blessed One, knowing it was Māra, spoke this verse to Māra: Excellent is the Muni, Living in an empty hut, Knowing how to…
content:
Then the Blessed One, knowing it was Māra, spoke this verse to Māra:

Excellent is the Muni,
Living in an empty hut,
Knowing how to tame himself,
There he abides.
Living having abandoned all,
With practice appropriate,
Many kinds of roaming beasts,
Many frightening things,
Many mosquitoes and poisonous snakes —
Not a single hair of the Muni
Living in the empty hut
Is disturbed.
Though the sky splits, the earth trembles,
Though all beings are terrified,
Though spears, swords, and arrows
Are thrown at his chest,
Buddhas do not create
Bases for attachment.

title: Bhikkhus, I eat only one meal a day. Bhikkhus, by eating only one meal a day, I feel free from disease, free from affliction, lightness,…
content: Bhikkhus, I eat only one meal a day. Bhikkhus, by eating only one meal a day, I feel free from disease, free from affliction, lightness, strength, and a pleasant abiding. Bhikkhus, you too should eat only one meal a day. Bhikkhus, by eating only one meal a day, you too will feel free from disease, free from affliction, lightness, strength, and a pleasant abiding.

title: - It is wonderful, Venerable Kaccāna, it is marvelous, Venerable Kaccāna, how Venerable Kaccāna has defined non-guarding of the faculties. Guarding of the faculties, guarding…
content: - It is wonderful, Venerable Kaccāna, it is marvelous, Venerable Kaccāna, how Venerable Kaccāna has defined non-guarding of the faculties. Guarding of the faculties, guarding of the faculties, Venerable Kaccāna has said. To what extent, Venerable Kaccāna, is there guarding of the faculties?" - "Here, brahmin, when a bhikkhu sees a form with the eye, his mind does not incline toward agreeable forms nor recoil from disagreeable forms; he lives with mindfulness established, with an immeasurable mind. He truly understands the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom. Therefore, the evil, unwholesome states that have arisen are completely abandoned without remainder. ... when he hears a sound ... smells an odor ... tastes a taste ... feels a touch ... when he cognizes a mind-object with the mind, his mind does not incline toward agreeable mind-objects nor recoil from disagreeable mind-objects; he lives with mindfulness established, with an immeasurable mind. He truly understands the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom. Therefore, the evil, unwholesome states that have arisen are completely abandoned without remainder. Thus, brahmin, is guarding of the faculties.
